title: Part Ten: Retirement: From Pension to 401(k)

sections.brief: DB vs DC defined; Studebaker 1963 (8,500+ lost benefits; 4,000 got ~15%); ERISA 2 Sept 1974 and PBGC (926,000 retirees, 30m insured; no employer required to offer a plan); Revenue Act 6 Nov 1978 s.401(k) effective 1980, IRS proposal 10 Nov 1981, 'never intended to replace DB'; DOL EBSA active participants DB 27.2m/DC 11.2m (1975), crossover 1984, 11.1m/96.4m (2023), DB share 71% to 10% across 2004 definition break; ICI industry-composition account; BLS 2026 access 72/52, DB 14%, DC 70%, state-local DB 86%; lowest decile 38/15; Vanguard median $44,115 vs mean $167,970, participation by income 43% to 95%; SCF 54.9% hold, conditional median $106,000; fees (ICI 0.76% to 0.26%; DOL 28% illustration, 'a third' claim rated mostly false; ~$16bn/yr arithmetic); auto-enrolment 94% vs 64%, SECURE 2.0 s.101, 17 state auto-IRAs; DOL alternative-assets proposal 30 Mar 2026 (status: proposed); labelled Interpretation with counter-readings. Figures: time; stats; money

Design 1935–1972 (first monthly cheque 1940, automatic COLA from 1975, SSI); financing (91.3% payroll tax); 2027 COLA 3.6%, average benefit $2,088 to $2,163; old-age poverty 35.2% (1959) to 9.9% (2024); 28.8m out of SPM poverty; 1983 amendments (FRA 67, taxation of benefits, federal employees); cap $184,500/$192,300, 90% (1982) to 81% (2021) of covered wages taxed; 2026 Trustees (9 June): OASI Q4 2032, OASDI Q3 2034, 83% then 65% payable, deficit 3.82 to 4.42% and its causes incl.
